summary: Frontend-only testing of SIGNALIS-OS (vanilla JS + custom Python server on localhost:8000) with Playwright. Covered: (1) new mobile hamburger menu + drawer (visibility, contents, touch targets, 3 close paths, 5 actions, notification preference checkboxes + localStorage persistence), (2) desktop hiding of the hamburger, (3) the ARIS-9 empty/truncated-response bug fix (_parseAction with nested/balanced JSON, preText capture, _cleanFinalResponse, empty-model fallback) validated both in isolation and end-to-end through the terminal with a stubbed /api/ollama/chat, (4) regressions for notifications, macros and workspaces tools. 24/24 functional assertions passed; no console errors observed. Only cosmetic/mobile-layout and testability observations remain.

ui_bugs.issue: Terminal input row is partially hidden/clipped behind the taskbar: window occupies y=64..788 while the taskbar wraps to two lines on mobile (~y>=760), so the prompt/input line is cut. User can still type but the field is only half visible.

No data-testid attributes anywhere in index.html or js/* (0 occurrences). Tests had to rely on ids/data-drawer-action/data-pref. Add data-testid to hamburger button, drawer, drawer buttons, pref checkboxes, terminal input/output and toasts.

issues: #mobile-drawer uses display:none -> .open{display:flex}, which cancels the transform slide transition (drawer pops in instead of sliding). Use visibility/pointer-events instead of display to keep the animation.
Drawer has no focus trap and focus is not moved into the drawer on open, nor returned to the hamburger on close (a11y).
[agent] stage lines and the '.dim' hint lines have very low contrast against the dark background (barely readable in screenshots).
#titlebar-title text is also very low contrast.

action_items: Fix mobile layout: terminal window height/bottom offset must account for the wrapped 2-row taskbar so the input row is fully visible at 390x844.
Optional: replace display:none/flex toggle on #mobile-drawer with visibility+transform so the slide-in transition actually animates.
Optional a11y: move focus into drawer on open, trap focus, restore focus to #mobile-menu-btn on close.
Optional: add data-testid attributes to interactive elements (drawer buttons, pref checkboxes, terminal input, toasts).
Optional: raise contrast of .t-dim / [agent] stage lines and #titlebar-title.
critical_code_review_comments: _parseAction / _extractBalancedJson / _cleanFinalResponse verified correct: nested objects, arrays, braces inside strings and escapes are all handled; preText is returned and surfaced via window.__onAgentPreText; residual ACTION/ARGS/OBSERVATION blocks are fully stripped (no leftover JSON). Empty model output falls back to '*Processamento concluído.*' instead of an empty bubble.

browser.workspace.save and macro.save slugify the provided name (lowercase, spaces->_): 'TEST_trab' is stored/returned as 'test_trab'. Intentional key normalization, but the original display name is lost — consider storing a separate displayName if UI should show the user's casing.

macro.list / browser.workspace.list return steps/urls as counts (numbers) rather than the arrays; full nested data is only available in localStorage. Fine as a summary, but callers must not expect arrays.
js/agent.js top-level function declarations (_parseAction, agentSend, ...) leak into global scope; consider an IIFE with an explicit window.aris9Agent namespace.
Drawer action handlers call close() before awaiting _quickList; works today but ordering is fragile if animations are added.
seed_data_creation: localStorage-only test data created in the browser profile: workspaces 'test_trab' and 'test_e2e'; macros 'test_x' and 'test_ui'. No server-side data touched.

rca_of_the_issue: The reported empty/truncated ARIS-9 responses were caused by the old non-greedy ARGS regex (broke on nested JSON), leftover ACTION/ARGS fragments after cleaning, and prose before ACTION being discarded. All three fixes are verified working: balanced-brace JSON extraction (string/escape aware), full block removal in _cleanFinalResponse, and preText emission rendered in the terminal. Additionally the empty-response nudge/fallback path was exercised and never yields an empty message.
